stated: Invest in renewable power to ensure that 90% of the UK’s electricity is generated from renewables by 2030, removing restrictions on solar and wind power and supporting tidal/wave power.

source.quote: Invest in renewable power so that 90% of the UK’s electricity is generated from renewables by 2030. Accelerate the deployment of renewable power and deliver energy security by: Removing the Conservatives’ unnecessary restrictions on new solar and wind power, and supporting investment and innovation in tidal and wave power in particular.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets emissions trajectory and clean energy generation, shifting the electricity mix away from fossil fuels and materially affecting the UK's climate and air quality pathway.

Large-scale renewable build-out affects household energy bills (a core O2 indicator) — direction contested but non-negligible: renewables can lower long-run costs but require upfront infrastructure investment that may affect bills in the near term.

Infrastructure investment at this scale has a genuine dual-horizon effect on productivity (energy as a business input), economic opportunity in emerging clean-energy industries, and long-run living standards via energy-cost and energy-security improvements.

membership_note: Three fundamentals cleared the non-negligible bar: the policy's primary target (O6 — emissions/climate), its direct price channel (O2 — energy bills as a cost-of-living indicator), and its broader economic investment effect (O13 — productivity and long-run living standards). Fiscal effects (O12) were considered but the policy's mechanism leans on removing restrictions and enabling private investment rather than a clearly material public spending pledge, so O12 is not included. O14 (distributional incidence of energy costs) was considered but falls within O2's cost-of-living scope for this policy's level of specificity.
